key_insight: The paper proposes moving critical coordination rules from software into FPGA hardware to make heterogeneous autonomous systems more deterministic, bounded, and safer in real time.
engineering_relevance: This is relevant for safety-critical autonomous platforms because hardware-enforced coordination can provide guaranteed latency, authorization, and synchronization where software-only orchestration may be too unpredictable.
method: Use the TB-CSPN framework to separate semantic reasoning from interaction management.
Map selected coordination semantics to FPGA primitives as a hardware-native layer.
Enforce temporal synchronization, semantic gating, and authorization constraints directly in hardware.
evidence_signal: The abstract presents a conceptual architecture rather than reporting experimental data, benchmarks, or quantitative evaluation.
watch_item: A key implementation concern is the complexity of selecting which coordination semantics are safe and practical to hardwire without reducing flexibility or increasing verification burden.
paper_title: Hardware-Enforced Semantic Coordination for Safety-Critical Real-Time Autonomous Systems
